Hi Talia —

Thanks again for walking through the usage patterns yesterday. Per our call, I pulled together two practical paths for Medsure if you want the ability to (a) upgrade temporarily for high-volume clinical windows and then swap back, or (b) do a staged downgrade while preserving critical features.

Quick summary:
- Upgrade window: Reserved throughput bump for a calendar month with a step-down swapback period (30 days) where you return to baseline and receive proportional credits.
- Downgrade cascade: A staged downgrade that retires optional modules first (analytics export, advanced reranking) and keeps core inference/SLAs intact; swapback allowed within 45 days but discounted credits reduce over time.

I've attached a draft MA plan that maps your current modules to the package matrix and a spreadsheet that outlines the swapback math across three scenarios.

Open questions we flagged from the call:
1) Which months are most likely for high-volume spikes? (clinics vs. corporate events)
2) Do you need feature-level continuity (e.g., analytics exports) during the downgrade window?
3) Is procurement looking for a firm cap on overage exposure or a credit-first approach?

If you want, I can put together a customer-facing summary with the exact dollar math for legal/procurement. Ben / Karthik — tagging you for pricing and technical constraints.

Thanks,
Irene

Thanks — tagging pricing details here so procurement has numbers to work off.

Talia / Medsure procurement — short answers below and I'll fold into a one-page appendix:

- Swapback credit model: For a full-month reserved bump we credit back pro-rata for any unused reserved seat-days during the 30-day swapback window. Simple example: reserve 100 seat-days for August, use 70 => 30 credited as $$ (formula in spreadsheet).
- Hard overage cap: we can set a soft cap with notification at 80% usage and a hard cap that's an absolute dollar limit; if you want a true hard stop we can implement throttling but customers typically prefer crediting + alerts.
- Change order vs amendment: standard practice — upgrades handled via statement-of-work amendment (DocuSign), swapbacks that only adjust future billing can be handled via an internal amendment without a separate signed change if both parties agree; procurement typically prefers a signed amendment to reduce ambiguity.

Karthik — any technical constraints about preserving the embedding export while downgrading the analytics module? I want to ensure the downgrade cascade keeps the export pipeline intact.

Ben

Quick technical note from infra: we can guarantee embedding export continuity if you keep the storage retention SKU and export connector enabled. The downgrade cascade should strip the analytics UI and scheduled rerank jobs first — that avoids any pipeline interruptions.

Operational caveats:
- If you downgrade during an active export job the job will complete but scheduled jobs are paused until re-enablement.
- Swapback implementation will re-provision reserved instances; there is a 24–48 hour window for capacity assignment during high-demand months (we recommend scheduling swapbacks 72 hours ahead of planned spikes).

I'll add a short appendix to the technical side of the proposal describing the exact flags to keep enabled for no-loss of exports.
